title: Annotatio V §.III: Selneccer — natural of elements; supernatural of body; spiritual of fruit — triple
pass_a_gloss: For so Nicol. Selneccerus asks in a short booklet on the Lord’s Supper: How manifold is eating, he says, in the Sacred Supper? and answers: Since Christ takes bread, breaks it, hands it to the disciples, and Paul says: As often as you shall eat this bread &c., it is manifest that a natural and physical Eating is to be posited — not of Christ’s body or blood, but of the elements, bread and wine. For these elements are not transubstantiated into Christ’s body and blood, but retain their nature, are digested, cooked, and consumed. But since not only bread is eaten in the Supper, but Christ says of the bread: Take, eat, this is my Body, therefore a supernatural and heavenly eating is to be posited, which is invisible and insensible, and yet an eating of Christ’s true and Substantial body according to Christ’s Institution words. And because a promise is added to the Institution words, because the application of Christ’s benefits is made by faith unto eternal life and salvation, therefore Spiritual eating also necessarily has place, and so a triple Eating can piously and truly be posited: Natural or physical Eating, which pertains to the visible and sensible elements, bread and wine; Sacramental Eating, which is to be referred to Christ’s true body and blood, which with the bread is exhibited and received, and which with the wine is given and drunk; And Spiritual Eating, which is to be understood only of the fruit and efficacy of salutary reception.
pass_b_english: Selneccer’s short booklet on the Lord’s Supper asks how manifold eating is and answers with a triple: natural/physical of the elements (bread and wine keep their nature, are digested); supernatural/heavenly of Christ’s true substantial body (invisible, per Institution); spiritual of the fruit and efficacy of salutary reception by faith.
So: Natural, Sacramental, and Spiritual — piously and truly posited.
source_text: Sic enim quærit Nicol. Selneccerus, in libello brevi de Cœna Domini: Quotuplex est manducatio, ait, in S. Cœna? & respondet: Cum Christus panem sumat, frangat porrigat discipulis, & Paulus dicat: Quotiescunque manducabitis panem hunc &c. manifestum est, Manducationem naturalem & physicam ponendam esse, non corporis aut sanguinis Christi, sed elementorum, panis & vini. Hæc enim elementa non transsubstantiantur in corpus & sanguinem Christi, sed naturam suam retinent, digeruntur, & coquuntur, & absumuntur. Cùm verò non tantum panis manducetur in Cœna, Sed Christus de pane dicat: Accipite, edite, hoc est Corpus meum, ideo manducatio supernaturalis & cælestis ponenda est, quæ est invisibilis & insensibilis, & tamen veri & Substantialís corporis Christi manducatio juxta verba institutionis Christi. Et quia promissio addita est verbis Institutionis, quia beneficiorum Christi applicatio fit per fidem, ad vitam & salutem æternam, ideò & Spiritualis manducatio locum necessariò habet, & ita triplex Manducatio piè & verè poni potest: Manducatio Naturalis, seu physica, quæ ad elementa visibilia & sensibilia, panem & vinum pertinet: Manducatio Sacramentalis, quæ ad verum corpus & sanguinem Christi, quod cum pane exhibetur & accipitur, & qui cum vino datur & bibitur, referenda est: Et Manducatio Spiritualis, quæ tantum est de fructu, & efficacia salutaris sumtionis intelligenda.
